name: Wa'lah ibn al-Harith
bio: Wa'lah ibn al-Harith was of Jarm, a Quda'ite tribe settled in the northern Sarat of the Yaman. Lyall notes that the text calls the author al-Harith ibn Wa'lah, but that the correct name appears to be as given above.
In the battle of al-Kulab the Second he was standard-bearer of the confederacy of Madhhij under 'Abd-Yaghuth.

poems.title: Ode XXXII: My mother and aunt bear the
poems.author: Wa'lah ibn al-Harith
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Wa'lah son of al-Harith, of Jarm.
poems.text:
My mother and aunt bear the ills of you twain, feet of mine, for what ye did at Kulab, when the heels were nigh cut off!

Yea, when I saw the foe's horse charging us troop after troop, I knew that the day was desperate, all but life quite lost.

I saved myself by a flight such as none had seen before, as though 'twere an eagle swooping in Taiman down on his prey—

A black eagle brownish of hue, whose feathers a steady rain has matted, some day of cold and storm [in the mountain air].

It seemed, when at last I put Hudhunnah between me and them, we were ostriches all in a string before a horseman's pursuit.

Let whoso will look for kindness and ruth from men of Tamim— no tie of kin nor of friend binds Jarm at least to Tamim !

I heard the horsemen behind shouting Muqa'is their cry, and straight there rose in my chest a stifling heat to my throat ;

Yea, if I can help it, Muqa'is shall not get hold of me : I shall not be made the show there of tent or village folk ;

I shall not be given to guard me a jailoress of Mudar, whose daily care is to feed her brood [and leave me to starve] !

I said to the man of Nahd — ' I pray thee mount me behind ' ! but how should a broken man mount thee — thy mother weep for her son !

I prayed him by all the bonds of kinship between us twain— but time was when Nahd and Jarm shunned each the other in hate.
